sections.name: Meter
sections.title: Ten-block meter drawing
sections.what: Clamps the number, works out how many of the ten blocks to fill, draws the label and value text, and sets the accessible values as whole percentages.
sections.why: Likely reason: a compact display that screen readers can also read.
sections.watch_out: The screen reader percentage and the ten blocks are rounded separately, so they can disagree slightly.

summary: A ten-block bar showing a number between 0 and 1, with its written value beside it.
purpose: Gives a quick visual sense of a value such as leverage, which is how much a call matters.
why: The comment calls it a leverage meter with an accessible meter role and a text value. Reason for the ten blocks is not stated.
how: Clamps the value to the range 0 to 1, rounds it to a count out of ten, draws ten blocks with the filled ones marked, and sets accessible values as whole percentages.
inputs: label (the name), value (a number from 0 to 1), valueText (the words shown beside the bar).
outputs: A meter element on screen. Nothing is stored.
risks: Blocks are rounded to tenths, so small differences do not show. A bad value is silently clamped, so it looks like 0 or full.
debug: If a bar looks empty when it should not, check the value passed in. If the text is wrong, check valueText, which is shown as given.
